title: Daily Life - He's not a Good Fit
audio: mp3/35. Daily Life - He's not a Good Fit.mp3

segments.zh: 各位英语学习者，大家好。

segments.en: And we're going to be looking at an office lesson today.
segments.zh: 我们今天要看的是一节关于办公室的课程。

segments.en: We've got a lesson about describing somebody who's not such a good employee.
segments.zh: 我们这节课要教大家如何描述一个不太称职的员工。

segments.en: So we're going to be talking about how to describe this type of situation and language for making your point.
segments.zh: 所以我们将讨论如何描述这种情况和语言来表达你的观点。

segments.en: So let's look at some vocabulary from the dialogue in Vocabulary Preview.
segments.zh: 所以让我们看看词汇预览中对话中的一些词汇。

segments.en: The first one is a good fit.
segments.zh: 第一个是 a good fit。

segments.en: So when we're talking about an employee and he's a good fit, it means he's suitable for the job.
segments.zh: 因此，当我们谈论员工并且他非常适合时，这意味着他适合这份工作。

segments.en: He's suitable for the job or for the company.
So the opposite would be not a good fit.
segments.zh: 所以相反的情况是不合适的。

segments.en: And our last word for Vocabulary Preview, performance.
segments.zh: 以及词汇预览的最后一个词：performance（工作表现）。

segments.en: How good or bad you do your job.
So you can have good performance or bad performance.
segments.zh: 所以你可以有好的表现或坏的表现。

segments.en: Just how well you do your job.
So now we're ready to listen to our dialogue for the first time and as always, it's going to be at a normal speed, but you don't have to worry about it.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们已经准备好第一次听我们的对话了，而且一如既往，它会以正常的速度，但你不必担心。

segments.en: Because we'll come back and explain all the key language.
segments.zh: 因为我们会回来解释所有关键语言。

segments.en: Now we're going to listen as two managers discuss the performance of one employee.
segments.zh: 现在我们将在两位经理讨论一名员工的表现时倾听。

segments.en: So Lauren, I just wanted to talk to you quickly about our new customer support representative, Jason Huntley.
segments.zh: 劳伦，我想跟你谈谈新来的客户支持专员杰森·亨特利。

segments.en: Basically, I've got a few concerns about him.
And the bottom line is, I don't think he's a good fit for our company.
segments.zh: 说到底，我觉得他不适合我们公司。

segments.en: I thought you were pleased with his overall performance.
segments.zh: 我以为你对他的整体表现感到满意。

segments.en: Didn't you just tell me last week how impressed you were with his attitude?
segments.zh: 上周你不是刚刚告诉我你对他的态度印象深刻吗？

segments.en: Yeah, his attitude is great, but he's really unreliable.
segments.zh: 没错，他态度很好，但做事很不靠谱。

segments.en: Sometimes he's really productive, but then other times...
segments.zh: 有时候效率很高，可有时候又……

segments.en: He was 45 minutes late for our morning meeting.
segments.zh: 他在我们早上的会议上迟到了 45 分钟。

segments.en: Well, I'm sure he had a perfectly good reason.
segments.zh: 我相信他一定有正当理由。

segments.en: But that's not the only thing.
You know, he really doesn't have the best work ethic.
segments.zh: 他的工作态度实在不怎么样。

segments.en: I'm constantly catching him on MSN and Facebook when he should be talking to clients.
segments.zh: 本该跟客户沟通时，我却老是看见他在用MSN和Facebook。

segments.en: As if you don't check Facebook at work.
segments.zh: 说得好像你上班从来不刷Facebook一样。

segments.en: We've invested a lot of time and money in his training.
segments.zh: 我们花了很多时间和钱培训他。

segments.en: So now it's up to you to coach him.
segments.zh: 现在该由你来好好指导他了。

segments.en: You would say that, wouldn't you?
Making me hire his stupid, useless cousin.
segments.zh: 还逼我雇他那个又笨又没用的亲戚。

segments.en: So apparently, Lauren hired her cousin.
segments.zh: 显然，劳伦雇了她的表弟。

segments.en: That's always a complicated situation working with family members.
segments.zh: 和家人一起工作，情况总是很复杂。

segments.en: Yeah, it makes it really difficult for Jeff, doesn't it?
segments.zh: 是的，这对杰夫来说真的很困难，不是吗？

segments.en: Yeah, and apparently Jeff isn't very happy.
segments.zh: 是的，显然杰夫不是很开心。

segments.en: Well, let's look at the language he used to tell us that he's unhappy about this.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们看看他用来告诉我们他对此不满意的语言。

segments.en: Okay, the first word on language takeaway today.
segments.zh: 好的，今天关于语言要点的第一个字。

segments.en: So, let's listen to some examples of unreliable so then you can understand what it means.
segments.zh: 所以，让我们听听一些不可靠的例子，这样你就可以理解它的含义。

segments.en: The trains here are so unreliable.
segments.zh: 这里的火车太不靠谱了。
他们永远不会准时到达。

segments.en: He never finishes his projects on time.
segments.zh: 他从来没有按时完成他的项目。

segments.en: You promised you would pick me up from work today.
segments.zh: 你答应你今天会来接我。

segments.en: We can understand that if someone is unreliable, we can't trust them to do their job, right?
segments.zh: 我们可以理解，如果一个人不可靠，我们就不能相信他们做他们的工作，对吧？

segments.en: So you don't want to be unreliable.
When you're productive, it means that you accomplish your job, right?
segments.zh: 当你富有成效时，这意味着你完成了你的工作，对吧？

segments.en: You do a lot of work in a short amount of time.
segments.zh: 你在很短的时间内完成了很多工作。

segments.en: You want to be a productive employee.
segments.zh: 你想成为一名富有成效的员工。
我们的第三个词，职业道德。

segments.en: So a person's work ethic is that person's attitude towards work.
segments.zh: 所以一个人的职业道德就是那个人对工作的态度。

segments.en: If they have a good work ethic, then they are always hardworking and they come to work early and they finish their jobs on time and they stay and do lots of overtime.
segments.zh: 如果他们有良好的职业操守，就会一直很勤奋，很早就来上班，按时完成工作，还会留下来加很多班。

segments.en: So that's a good work ethic.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种很好的职业道德。
还有我们最后一个词：coach（指导）。

segments.en: When you coach an employee, you train them, right?
segments.zh: 当你指导员工时，你对他们进行培训，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, you help that employee out by showing him or her how to do certain tasks.
segments.zh: 是的，您通过向他或她展示如何完成某些任务来帮助该员工。

segments.en: Or how to do their job better.
segments.zh: 或者如何更好地完成他们的工作。

segments.en: So we've got some great language to describe work performance.
segments.zh: 所以我们有一些很棒的语言来描述工作表现。

segments.en: Let's listen to our dialogue a second time.
segments.zh: 让我们再听一次我们的对话。

segments.en: This time it'll be a little bit slower so you can understand these words and phrases a little bit more clearly.
segments.zh: 这次会慢一点，这样你就可以更清楚地理解这些单词和短语。

segments.zh: 让我雇用你愚蠢、无用的表弟。

segments.zh: 好吧，如果你注意到了，出现了很多有用的短语。

segments.zh: 三个短语可以帮助我们更好地说明我们的观点。

Let's listen to how this was used in the dialogue.

segments.en: And the bottom line is, I don't think he's a good fit for our company.
segments.zh: 说到底，我觉得他不适合我们公司。

segments.en: And the bottom line is, I don't think he's a good fit for our company.
segments.zh: 说到底，我觉得他不适合我们公司。
我们的第二个词，总体而言。

segments.en: So this is the same as saying on the whole.
segments.zh: 这和 on the whole（总体上）是一个意思。

segments.en: So it's a big picture, how you would say.
So his overall performance is good.

segments.zh: 我们最后一个短语很有意思，因为我们可以稍微变一下。

一个完全说得通的理由。

segments.en: So by the sounds of it, it's kind of like justifying.
